ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: G*Power menu option changed — must know specific G*Power interface options
ground_truth.original_snippet: The option used in G*Power was 'ANOVA: Repeated measures, within-between interaction'.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: The option used in G*Power was 'ANOVA: Repeated measures, within-between'.
ground_truth.description: Removed 'interaction' from G*Power option — computes power for main effects test not the interaction that tests the core hypothesis

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Counterbalancing removed — must know item confounds are fatal for within-subjects discussed/not-discussed comparison
ground_truth.original_snippet: In order to counterbalance the discussed details, 50% of the pairs will discuss different critical details than the other 50% of the pairs. For example, half the pairs will talk about Eric's cap color but without discussing his company logo (version A of the discussion), while the other pairs will d...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase. For example, all pairs will talk about Eric's cap color and his company logo.
ground_truth.description: Removed item counterbalancing — without it, discussed vs non-discussed comparison confounds item difficulty with experimental manipulation

matched_finding.subcategory: discussed items not counterbalanced despite claim
matched_finding.description: The design section claims discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced, but the procedure states that every pair will discuss the same four critical details. This confounds discussion status with item identity: any differences between discussed and non-discussed items may reflect inherent item difficulty, memorability, or salience rather than memory conformity.
matched_finding.quote: "discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced" ... "In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase."

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Disputed/non-disputed classification removed — must know not all discussed items contain misinformation
ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize participants’ answers into two groups: "disputed" and "non-disputed". More precisely, if a pair of participants disagreed with each other and gave d...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In addition, while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s ...
ground_truth.description: Removed disputed/non-disputed classification — treats all discussed items as containing misinformation when some may not have; conflates delivered vs non-delivered misinformation

matched_finding.description: The collaborative discussion may not actually expose a participant to the partner’s discrepant version. Partners may guess, say they do not know, provide the participant’s version, or fail to disclose the discrepant detail. Yet the analysis plan proposes categorizing all discussed items as containing misinformation. This creates misclassification of exposure and biases estimates of memory conformity and intervention effects.
matched_finding.quote: "If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented."; "we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner’s differing version of events."

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Pre vs post misinformation intervention — must understand encoding vs retrieval distinction
ground_truth.original_snippet: we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation after the collaborative recall phase (that is, after exposing participants to misinformation). The main reason for that is that we wanted to make our research closer to real life settings. In reality, one rarely has a chance to do...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation). The main reason for that is that we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take eff...
ground_truth.description: Changed intervention from post- to pre-misinformation — tests encoding prevention instead of retrieval resistance; invalidates IMP theoretical framework which requires post-exposure placement

matched_finding.description: The manuscript gives contradictory descriptions of when the three reduction procedures occur. The introduction states that the methods will be placed before collaborative recall, but the methods section’s four-phase procedure places collaborative recall before the procedures. The detailed procedure also administers the interventions after the discussion and filler task. This is a critical design inconsistency because intervention timing is central to the theoretical rationale, causal mechanism, and comparability with prior warning studies.
matched_finding.quote: "What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation)." ... "The procedure will consist of four main phases: (1) presenting the original material, (2) collaborative recall (including misinformation), (3) three procedures to reduce vulnerability to misinformation (and a control condition), and (4) an individual memory test of the original material."

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Directional tests but sample sizes match two-tailed — must verify power calculation assumptions
ground_truth.original_snippet: Comparisons among all groups and non-directional significance tests are assumed.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'non-directional' to 'directional' — reported sample sizes (492, 82, 34) are for two-tailed tests; one-tailed would need smaller N, creating inconsistency

matched_finding.subcategory: directional tests despite possible bidirectional effects
matched_finding.description: The manuscript acknowledges that education or demonstration of memory fallibility may increase suggestibility, yet assumes directional significance tests for intervention effects. A one-tailed test is not justified when plausible and theoretically discussed effects exist in the opposite direction.
matched_finding.quote: "increased memory conformity is possible."; "Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed."

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Hypothesis awareness exclusion removed — must know this is critical in deception paradigms
ground_truth.original_snippet: Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. If any of the participants correctly guesses our hypotheses, they will be excluded from the analysis and replaced with another person in order to maintain the correct sample size. We realize that this may ...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis of any relationship between hypothesis awareness and performance.
ground_truth.description: Removed pre-registered exclusion of hypothesis-aware participants — critical safeguard in deception paradigm; also removed acknowledgment of differential exclusion risk

matched_finding.subcategory: possible contamination from hypothesis awareness question placement
matched_finding.description: The hypothesis-awareness question is administered only after the final memory test, so it cannot identify participants who became aware before or during interventions versus during the final test. It also cannot prevent awareness-induced changes in primary outcomes. Using it only exploratorily limits interpretability of deception failures.
matched_finding.quote: "Next, the subjects will be requested to say what they think the real purpose of the study was. Their responses will be recorded for exploratory analysis"

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Within-pair age matching removed — must know authority dynamics in memory conformity
ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, the age of the participants in each pair will be matched as far as possible.
ground_truth.description: Removed within-pair age matching — age differences activate authority/deference dynamics that inflate conformity through social influence rather than informational influence

matched_finding.subcategory: age range rationale insufficient and residual age confounding
matched_finding.description: Restricting age to 16–35 is justified by avoiding young–elderly dyads, but dyads within this range can still differ substantially in age and status, and age may influence conformity. The design does not specify age matching, recording dyad age differences, or controlling for them.
matched_finding.quote: "The age of the participants will be restricted in order to avoid a situation in which a very young participant would discuss the original material with an elderly one"

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: 'Completely ruled out' vs 'has little use' — must recognize experimenter-awareness caveat was theoretically important
ground_truth.original_snippet: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect has little use in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is little cost of disagreeing (although it is still possible that some pressure exists as the p...
ground_truth.modified_snippet: we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'has little use' to 'completely ruled out' and removed experimenter-awareness caveat — overclaims mechanism specificity

matched_finding.description: The authors claim normative impact is completely ruled out because the final test is individual. However, normative effects may operate during collaborative recall, through commitment to jointly agreed answers, perceived expectations, concern about consistency with the partner, or internalized social pressure. Dismissing this mechanism is unjustified and narrows interpretation improperly.
matched_finding.quote: "we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study: participants work on their own and do not compare their answers with anybody, therefore there is no cost of disagreeing."

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Open-ended→forced-choice changes baseline conformity rate and scoring categories — must know format matters
ground_truth.original_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will be in the form of open-ended questions.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.
ground_truth.description: Changed from open-ended to forced-choice — inflates conformity rates (50% guessing baseline vs much lower); scoring categories (correct, misinformation, other) don't make sense with forced-choice

matched_finding.description: The individual memory test is described in the procedure as open-ended, but the analysis plan later states that it will use a two-alternative forced-choice format. These formats measure different constructs, have different chance levels, require different scoring, and differ in susceptibility to response bias. The contradiction prevents evaluation or replication of the primary outcome.
matched_finding.quote: "The test will contain 20 open-ended questions" ... "In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format."

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Co-witness exposure exclusion removed — must know non-exposed participants dilute the effect
ground_truth.original_snippet: In addition, participants who are not exposed to co-witness details at all (that is, the participants who did not hear any potentially misleading information from the partner) will be excluded from the analyses.
ground_truth.description: Removed exclusion of non-exposed participants — including those who received zero misinformation dilutes the conformity effect and biases against finding both the basic effect and intervention benefit
